doc.title: Louie Bellson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: Bellson's arrangements Hawk Talks and Skin Deep and recording Skin Deep in a ballroom
summary: Duke records his charts; Skin Deep is recorded after a Fresno tape and in a ballroom on tour in 1951.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Didn’t they play some of your first charts?

When I joined the band, Tizol was telling Duke, “yeah this kid, he knows how to write, too.” He said “well tell him to bring an arrangement in.” I said “Tizol, no way, I’m not going to do that, not with him and Strayhorn around.” I was being just this high you know. So he had to ask me two or three times. So finally Tizol got a hold of “Hawk Talks” and “Skin Deep” and when Duke heard “Hawk Talks” they recorded it right off the bat.

I was just, you know, as a kid I couldn’t get over it. And it enjoyed some success as a jazz cut you know. And then later on we couldn’t find a studio in those days to record “Skin Deep,” because all that drumming, they couldn’t find a studio to get the clarity of all those fast beats that I was doing on “Skin Deep.” So Duke hesitated. He said “let’s wait on that one.” So while we were on the road, Burt Porter, who was one of the guys that brought in the Ampex hi-fi, he recorded the band one night in Fresno, California. And when Duke heard that, he said “okay, let’s record ‘Skin Deep.’” So we did that out on the coast, and then sent that tape into Columbia. And they wanted to know where we did that, because they said we couldn’t do anything like that you know. So if you study that cut real closely you’ll discover that “Skin Deep” sounded very different than the other things on that album. And that’s the reason why.
So it was recorded not in the studio, or was it recorded on location or something? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -8-

We had finished playing Fresno, that’s when we heard the recorded tape that Burt did, and we were on our way up to Seattle. Somewhere in there we played a ballroom and Duke liked the sound of the ballroom so he said “okay, let’s go down after the gig and do ‘Skin Deep.’” We did, and we lucked out.
Yeah. ‘51. 1951 I joined the band. Shortly after that we recorded “Hawk Talks” and “Skin Deep.” Yeah.
